notes: Synthetic negotiation. Ground truth = the disposition the playbook (03) dictates for each numbered change in the markup (02), plus the counter-position numbers where the disposition is COUNTER. One change (s.9.1 warranty 90 -> 180 days) is deliberately left unmarked in the markup.

dispositions.title: Payment terms Net 30 -> Net 45
evidence: [[DEL: thirty (30)]][[INS: forty-five (45)]] days after the invoice date
Net 45 is acceptable.
dispositions.model_answer: Net 45 is within playbook fallback P-1.

dispositions.title: Deletion of 1.5% monthly late-payment interest
evidence: Never delete late-payment interest entirely.
Late-payment interest may be reduced to 1.0% per month.
dispositions.model_answer: Reinstate s.4.2 at a reduced 1.0% per month (P-2).

dispositions.title: General liability cap 12 -> 36 months' fees
evidence: [[DEL: TWELVE (12)]][[INS: THIRTY-SIX (36)]]
The general liability cap may be increased to 24 months' fees.
dispositions.model_answer: Offer a 24 months' fees cap (P-3); 36 months exceeds the walk-away.

dispositions.title: Uncapped liability for Provider's breach of s.8 (Data Security)
evidence: PROVIDER'S BREACH OF SECTION 8 (DATA SECURITY)
Offer a separate super-cap for data-security breaches equal to 3x the annual Fees.
dispositions.model_answer: Replace the uncapped carve-out with a separate super-cap of 3x the annual Fees (P-4).

dispositions.title: New s.4.4 most-favored-customer pricing
evidence: Always reject most-favored-customer or price-parity clauses.
dispositions.model_answer: MFN pricing is a P-5 walk-away; strike s.4.4.

dispositions.title: Customer termination for convenience at any time on 30 days' notice
evidence: Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon thirty (30) days' written notice
Termination for convenience is acceptable only after the first 12 months of the Subscription Term, on at least 90 days' notice, with an early termination fee of 50% of the remaining Fees.
dispositions.position_title: only after 12 months, 90 days' notice, 50% early termination fee
dispositions.model_answer: Allow termination for convenience only after the first 12 months, on 90 days' notice, with an early termination fee of 50% of remaining Fees (P-6).

dispositions.title: Governing law Delaware -> New York
evidence: [[DEL: Delaware]][[INS: New York]]
New York law is an acceptable alternative.
dispositions.model_answer: New York law is an acceptable alternative under P-7.

dispositions.title: SLA service-credit cap 10% -> 25%
evidence: [[DEL: ten percent (10%)]][[INS: twenty-five percent (25%)]]
Service credits may be capped at up to 15% of monthly Fees.

dispositions.title: On-site audit at any time on 10 business days' notice
evidence: may conduct an on-site audit of Provider's facilities, systems and records relating to Customer Data at any time upon ten (10) business days' notice
On-site audits only once per 12 months, on 30 days' notice, and only following a confirmed Security Incident affecting Customer Data.
dispositions.position_title: once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, only after a Security Incident
dispositions.model_answer: Keep SOC 2 + questionnaire; allow on-site audits once per 12 months on 30 days' notice only after a confirmed Security Incident (P-9).

dispositions.title: Cyber insurance $2M -> $5M per claim
evidence: Cyber insurance limits of up to $5,000,000 per claim are acceptable.

dispositions.title: Customer may assign to any third party without consent
evidence: Customer may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any third party without Provider's consent
Unilateral free assignment by Customer.
dispositions.model_answer: Unilateral free assignment is a P-11 walk-away; keep mutual s.13.1.

dispositions.title: Non-renewal notice 60 -> 90 days
evidence: [[DEL: sixty (60)]][[INS: ninety (90)]] days before the end of the then-current term
A non-renewal notice period of up to 90 days is acceptable.
dispositions.model_answer: Up to 90 days is acceptable under P-12.

dispositions.title: Deletion of lost profits from the consequential-damages exclusion
evidence: [[DEL: , OR LOST PROFITS]]
Never remove lost profits from the mutual consequential-damages exclusion.
dispositions.model_answer: Removing lost profits from the exclusion is a P-13 walk-away; reinstate.

facts.title: Unmarked change: s.9.1 warranty period silently extended from 90 to 180 days
facts.question: What warranty period does the counterparty's latest draft of the MSA provide?
evidence: for a period of one hundred eighty (180) days after each release is made available to Customer
for a period of ninety (90) days after each release is made available to Customer
facts.model_answer: Section 9.1's warranty period was changed from 90 to 180 days but the change is unmarked in Corvane's markup; it must be called out, reversed to 90 days (P-14) and escalated.

facts.title: Unmarked change must be reversed to 90 days and escalated per the playbook integrity rule
facts.question: What does the playbook require when the counterparty makes a change without marking it?
evidence: Any change the counterparty did not mark must be called out to the counterparty in writing as an unmarked change, reversed, and escalated to the deal lead
facts.model_answer: Reverse the warranty period to ninety (90) days and escalate the unmarked change to the deal lead.
